transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I've just completed your post-cataract surgery follow-up check. 

Do you have any questions about your surgery or your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora. Yes, I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great question! You can start doing light gardening after 1 week from your surgery. However, you should avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise for about a month.

So gentle gardening is fine after that first week, but try to take it easy and avoid anything too demanding.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That sounds good, thank you. I do have another question. When can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Good question. If you were using eye gel for dry eyes before your surgery, it's safe to continue using it now, unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

If you need more of it, your GP should be able to provide some for you.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I see, thanks for the information. Yes, I have another question. I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you go outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to assess it further. In that case, it's best to contact your care team.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for explaining that, I appreciate it. I have one more question. Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. It's quite common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

How long has it been since your surgery? If your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything is okay.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for clarifying. It's been about a week since the surgery. I'll keep an eye on it and reach out if it's not improving. I don't have any more questions at the moment. Thank you for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's great! So just to confirm - have all your questions about your surgery and recovery been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, all my questions have been answered. Thanks so much for your help, Dora!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help. Take care and best wishes with your recovery!
